chunks: Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurara said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Is there anything (zakat) upon the mules?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. So I said, 'So how did it come to be upon the horses and not upon the mules?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Because the mules do not reproduce, and the female horses give birth, and there is nothing upon the male horses'. He said, 'So I said, 'So what is regarding the donkeys?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing with regards to them'. I said, 'Is there anything upon the horse, or the camel which the man happens to be riding upon?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, there is nothing upon what is fed (not grazing). Rather, the charity (zakat) is upon the grazing animal sent out in its pasture during its year which the man acquired. But, as for what is besides that, so there is nothing with regards to it'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on zakat for mules, horses, and donkeys in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that zakat is strictly limited to 'saimah' (grazing livestock) that are freely pasturing for a full lunar year, thereby exempting riding animals and those kept in stables. The distinction regarding mules highlights their sterility, while the ruling on horses and donkeys emphasizes that utility (riding) rather than species alone determines exemption. This hadith serves as a foundational text for Shia jurists in defining the specific conditions of ownership and grazing required for livestock zakat.
